topic: Cached benchmark speed versus cold-prompt reality
title: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash at 378 tok/s: the cache-hit catch
description: The Hacker News headline says DeepSeek v4.1 Flash writes at 378 tokens per second. That number is real, but it belongs to an agent running at a 99.7% cache hit rate, not to your first cold prompt. Here is what prefill costs you, and when the headline actually is yours. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: 378 tok/s has a catch: it isn't yours.
The benchmark that isn't about you.
Everyone read the number. Nobody read the method.
DeepSeek v4.1 Flash isn't that fast for you.
Cache hits made that number. You have none.
That benchmark is somebody else's warmup.
You'd pay the prefill. They didn't.
The speed is real. It just isn't yours.
narration_full: Three hundred seventy-eight tokens a second, and that speed isn't your speed. You saw the headline for DeepSeek four point one Flash. That number is RunInfra's, measuring the model alone, just the writing. Nearly every request it served was a repeat the model had already read. A cache hit is a prompt whose start matches notes already stored. One room, one brain, a desk for each conversation. That desk is the KV cache, the running notes of everything already read. Keeping notes for repeats is prefix caching. A hit finds your desk untouched. But the desk takes memory, and it doesn't last. Memory pressure clears it. DeepSeek clears its disk cache nightly. Your first prompt is a cache miss. It owes full prefill, a complete read before the first word is written. So what does your first prompt sit through? On DeepSeek's own API, a very long prompt took thirteen seconds to its first token. Warm, five hundred milliseconds. That gap is the cache. Whose speed is it? The traffic's, not the model's. Same model, same hardware, different requests. RunInfra's best account was an agent that had already read a very long prompt. The model doesn't make the hits. Your prompts do. Independent tests on DeepSeek's own API measured it slower. The number is real, and cache hits are how production agents run. Every new conversation repeats that first read. So measure the first prompt. That one is yours.
